bank.name: Inventions & Scientists
bank.subject: General Science & Ability
bank.description: Famous inventors, discoveries and the scientists behind them.

questions.prompt: Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was discovered by?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928.

questions.prompt: The law of gravitation was formulated by?
questions.explanation: Newton published the law of universal gravitation in 1687.

questions.prompt: The telephone was invented by?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876.

questions.prompt: The practical electric light bulb is credited to?
questions.explanation: Edison developed a commercially practical incandescent bulb in 1879.

questions.prompt: Wireless radio communication is associated with?
questions.explanation: Marconi developed practical wireless telegraphy/radio.

questions.prompt: X-rays were discovered by?
questions.explanation: Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.prompt: The periodic table of elements was developed by?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev published the first periodic table in 1869.

questions.prompt: The theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed by?
questions.explanation: Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species' (1859) proposed natural selection.

questions.prompt: The first vaccination (for smallpox) was developed by?
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner created the smallpox vaccine in 1796.

questions.prompt: Pasteurization, the process of heating liquids to kill microbes, is named after?
questions.explanation: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization.

questions.prompt: The double-helix structure of DNA was discovered by?
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick published the DNA model in 1953.

questions.prompt: Dolly, the first cloned mammal, was?
questions.explanation: Dolly the sheep was cloned in 1996.

questions.prompt: Radium and polonium were discovered by?
questions.explanation: The Curies discovered radium and polonium; Marie won two Nobel Prizes.

questions.prompt: The Nobel Prize is named after?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel, inventor of dynamite, endowed the prizes.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the father of modern physics?
questions.explanation: Einstein's theories of relativity transformed modern physics.

questions.prompt: Who invented the safety elevator?
questions.explanation: Elisha Otis invented the safety elevator in 1853.

questions.prompt: Marie Curie is famous for her work on:
questions.explanation: Curie discovered radium and polonium; she won two Nobel Prizes.

questions.prompt: Who invented the steam engine (improved version)?
questions.explanation: Watt's improved steam engine (1769) powered the Industrial Revolution.

questions.prompt: Who is credited with inventing the airplane?
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first powered flight in 1903.

questions.prompt: The polio vaccine was developed by:
questions.explanation: Salk developed the first effective polio vaccine in 1955.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the electron?
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897.

questions.prompt: Who invented the zipper?
questions.explanation: Gideon Sundback perfected the modern zipper in 1913.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the tuberculosis (TB) bacterium?
questions.explanation: Robert Koch identified the TB bacillus in 1882.

questions.prompt: Who built the steam locomotive 'Rocket'?
questions.explanation: George Stephenson's Rocket (1829) was a famous early locomotive.

questions.prompt: Who first observed the four largest moons of Jupiter?
questions.explanation: Galileo discovered Jupiter's large moons in 1610.

questions.prompt: Who is the father of modern chemistry?
questions.explanation: Lavoisier revolutionised chemistry with the law of conservation of mass.

questions.prompt: Who invented the telescope?
questions.explanation: Lippershey, a Dutch lensmaker, invented the telescope in 1608.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the circulation of blood?
questions.explanation: Harvey described blood circulation in 1628.

questions.prompt: Who invented the computer mouse?
questions.explanation: Engelbart demonstrated the mouse in 1968.

questions.prompt: Who invented the barometer?
questions.explanation: Torricelli invented the barometer in 1643.

questions.prompt: Who invented the helicopter?
questions.explanation: Sikorsky built the first practical helicopter in 1939.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the father of computers?
questions.explanation: Babbage designed the analytical engine, the first computer concept.

questions.prompt: Who invented the refrigerator?
questions.explanation: Perkins patented the first vapour-compression refrigerator in 1834.

questions.prompt: Who invented the ballpoint pen?
questions.explanation: Bíró patented the modern ballpoint pen in 1938.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the neutron?
questions.explanation: Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

questions.prompt: Who invented the battery?
questions.explanation: Volta invented the voltaic pile, the first battery, in 1800.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the laws of planetary motion?
questions.explanation: Kepler formulated his three laws of planetary motion.

questions.prompt: Who invented the motion picture camera?
questions.explanation: Edison's kinetoscope was an early motion picture camera.

questions.prompt: The first person to walk on the Moon was:
questions.explanation: Armstrong stepped onto the Moon in 1969 during Apollo 11.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the hormone insulin?
questions.explanation: Banting and Best isolated insulin in 1921.

questions.prompt: Who invented the internal combustion engine?
questions.explanation: Nikolaus Otto built the first practical four-stroke engine in 1876.

questions.prompt: Who invented the electric telegraph?
questions.explanation: Samuel Morse developed the electric telegraph and Morse code.

questions.prompt: Who developed the BCG vaccine against tuberculosis?
questions.explanation: Calmette and Guérin developed the BCG vaccine in 1921.

questions.prompt: The first artificial satellite was:
questions.explanation: The USSR launched Sputnik 1 in 1957.

questions.prompt: Who discovered radioactivity?
questions.explanation: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896.

questions.prompt: Who captured the famous X-ray diffraction image of DNA (Photo 51)?
questions.explanation: Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51 helped reveal the DNA double helix.

questions.prompt: Who invented the mechanical calculator known as the stepped reckoner?
questions.explanation: Gottfried Leibniz built the stepped reckoner in 1672.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the proton?
questions.explanation: Rutherford discovered the proton in 1919.

questions.prompt: The telescope was improved for astronomical use by:
questions.explanation: Galileo used telescopes to observe the heavens in 1609.

questions.prompt: The first vaccine was developed against:
questions.explanation: Jenner's 1796 vaccine targeted smallpox.

questions.prompt: The first successful heart transplant was performed by:
questions.explanation: Barnard performed the first human heart transplant in 1967.

questions.prompt: Who discovered oxygen?
questions.explanation: Priestley isolated oxygen in 1774; Lavoisier named it.

questions.prompt: The concept of the atom was first proposed in modern science by:
questions.explanation: Dalton's atomic theory (1808) founded modern chemistry.

questions.prompt: Who proposed the heliocentric model of the Solar System?
questions.explanation: Copernicus placed the Sun at the centre in 1543.

questions.prompt: The field of quantum mechanics was founded by:
questions.explanation: Planck's quantum theory (1900) started quantum mechanics.

questions.prompt: Who invented the modern air conditioner?
questions.explanation: Willis Carrier built the first modern air conditioner in 1902.

questions.prompt: Who invented the typewriter?
questions.explanation: Sholes patented the first practical typewriter in 1868.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the nucleus of the atom?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's gold-foil experiment revealed the nucleus in 1911.

questions.prompt: Who invented the diesel engine?
questions.explanation: Rudolf Diesel patented the diesel engine in 1892.

questions.prompt: The anaesthetic properties of ether were first demonstrated by:
questions.explanation: Long used ether for surgery in 1842.

questions.prompt: Who discovered Uranus?
questions.explanation: Herschel discovered Uranus in 1781.

questions.prompt: The inventor of the modern computer, the Analytical Engine, was:
questions.explanation: Babbage designed the Analytical Engine in the 1830s.

questions.prompt: Who invented the television?
questions.explanation: Baird demonstrated the first working television in 1925.

questions.prompt: The rabies and anthrax vaccines are attributed to:
questions.explanation: Pasteur pioneered vaccines for both rabies and anthrax.

questions.prompt: Who invented the phonograph?
questions.explanation: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph, the first sound recorder, in 1877.

questions.prompt: Who explained the photoelectric effect and won a Nobel Prize for it?
questions.explanation: Einstein explained the photoelectric effect, earning the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.prompt: Who co-founded Microsoft with Bill Gates?
questions.explanation: Paul Allen and Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft in 1975.

questions.prompt: Who first observed the rings of Saturn through a telescope?
questions.explanation: Galileo saw Saturn's rings in 1610, initially mistaking them for handles.

questions.prompt: Which astronomer defended the heliocentric model and was tried by the Inquisition?
questions.explanation: Galileo's telescopic evidence for heliocentrism led to his 1633 trial.

questions.prompt: Who invented the printing press?
questions.explanation: Johannes Gutenberg invented the movable-type printing press around 1440.

questions.prompt: Who invented the pendulum clock?
questions.explanation: Christiaan Huygens built the first pendulum clock in 1656.

questions.prompt: Who invented the sewing machine?
questions.explanation: Elias Howe patented the first practical sewing machine in 1846.

questions.prompt: Who invented the dynamite?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite in 1867.

questions.prompt: Who won Nobel Prizes in both Physics and Chemistry?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie won the Physics Prize (1903) and the Chemistry Prize (1911).

questions.prompt: Who discovered the laws of inheritance using pea plants?
questions.explanation: Gregor Mendel discovered the laws of inheritance through experiments on pea plants.

questions.prompt: The law of universal gravitation describes the force between:
questions.explanation: Universal gravitation is the attractive force acting between any two masses.

questions.prompt: The first man to travel into space was:
questions.explanation: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth in Vostok 1 in April 1961.

questions.prompt: Who invented the cotton gin?
questions.explanation: Eli Whitney invented the cotton gin in 1793.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the cell under a microscope?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke first described cells from a slice of cork in 1665.

questions.prompt: Who invented the safety matches?
questions.explanation: John Walker invented the first friction safety matches in 1826.

questions.prompt: The law of conservation of mass is associated with:
questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier established that mass is conserved in chemical reactions.

questions.prompt: The first computer programmer was:
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm intended for a machine.

questions.prompt: Who invented the laser?
questions.explanation: Theodore Maiman built the first working laser in 1960.

questions.prompt: Who is regarded as the father of computer science?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing is regarded as the father of computer science.

questions.prompt: Who independently proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.explanation: Alfred Russel Wallace independently conceived the theory of natural selection alongside Darwin.

questions.prompt: Who built the first mechanical calculating machine, the Pascaline?
questions.explanation: Blaise Pascal built the Pascaline, an early mechanical calculator, in 1642.

questions.prompt: Who invented the alternating current (AC) system?
questions.explanation: Nikola Tesla developed the alternating current (AC) system.

questions.prompt: Who invented the mercury thermometer?
questions.explanation: Fahrenheit made the first reliable mercury thermometer in 1714.

questions.prompt: Who invented the first compound microscope?
questions.explanation: Zacharias Janssen is credited with the first compound microscope around 1590.

questions.prompt: Who proposed the quantum theory of the atom?
questions.explanation: Bohr's 1913 model placed electrons in fixed orbits around the nucleus.

questions.prompt: Who proposed the 'plum pudding' model of the atom?
questions.explanation: Thomson pictured electrons embedded in a positive sphere, like plums in pudding.

questions.prompt: Who invented the lightning rod?
questions.explanation: Benjamin Franklin invented the lightning rod after his kite experiments.

questions.prompt: Who invented the photocopier (xerography)?
questions.explanation: Chester Carlson invented xerography in 1938; Xerox commercialised it.

questions.prompt: Who invented the postage stamp?
questions.explanation: Rowland Hill introduced the Penny Black, the first adhesive postage stamp.

questions.prompt: Who invented the gramophone?
questions.explanation: Emile Berliner's gramophone played flat discs, unlike Edison's cylinder phonograph.

questions.prompt: Who invented the microwave oven?
questions.explanation: Percy Spencer discovered microwave heating from a radar magnetron in 1945.

questions.prompt: Who invented the first automatic traffic light?
questions.explanation: Garrett Morgan patented a three-position traffic signal in 1923.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the father of the atomic bomb?
questions.explanation: Robert Oppenheimer directed the Manhattan Project that built the atomic bomb.

questions.prompt: Who invented the spinning jenny?
questions.explanation: James Hargreaves invented the spinning jenny during the Industrial Revolution.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the noble gases?
questions.explanation: William Ramsay isolated argon, helium and the other noble gases.

questions.prompt: Who invented the safety razor?
questions.explanation: King Gillette invented the safety razor with disposable blades.

questions.prompt: Who invented the mechanical reaper?
questions.explanation: Cyrus McCormick's reaper transformed wheat harvesting in the 1830s.

questions.prompt: Who invented the first bicycle (the draisine)?
questions.explanation: Karl von Drais built the draisine, a two-wheeled runabout, in 1817.

questions.prompt: Who built the first practical automobile with an internal combustion engine?
questions.explanation: Karl Benz built the Motorwagen in 1885, widely considered the first automobile.

questions.prompt: Who invented the automated teller machine (ATM)?
questions.explanation: John Shepherd-Barron installed the first ATM in London in 1967.

questions.prompt: Who made the first mobile phone call?
questions.explanation: Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld mobile call in 1973.

questions.prompt: Who first observed the planet Neptune through a telescope?
questions.explanation: Johann Galle found Neptune in 1846 at the position predicted by Le Verrier.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the dwarf planet Pluto?
questions.explanation: Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto at Lowell Observatory in 1930.

questions.prompt: Who discovered Saturn's largest moon, Titan?
questions.explanation: Huygens discovered Titan in 1655, about forty years before Cassini's moons.

questions.prompt: Who invented the reflecting telescope?
questions.explanation: Newton built the first practical reflecting telescope in 1668 using a mirror.

questions.prompt: Who is credited with inventing the jet engine?
questions.explanation: Frank Whittle patented the turbojet engine in 1930.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Valentina Tereshkova orbited the Earth in 1963 aboard Vostok 6.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie won the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the ABO blood group system?
questions.explanation: Karl Landsteiner identified the A, B and O blood groups in 1900.

questions.prompt: Who invented the stethoscope?
questions.explanation: Rene Laennec invented the stethoscope in 1816.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the father of medicine?
questions.explanation: Hippocrates, the Greek physician, is called the father of medicine.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the father of biology?
questions.explanation: Aristotle is regarded as the father of biology for his study of living things.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the father of taxonomy?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus devised the binomial system of naming species.

questions.prompt: Who first observed bacteria under a microscope?
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek, the father of microbiology, first saw bacteria in 1674.

questions.prompt: Who invented the pressure cooker?
questions.explanation: Denis Papin's steam digester of 1679 was the forerunner of the pressure cooker.

questions.prompt: Who invented the integrated circuit?
questions.explanation: Jack Kilby built the first working integrated circuit at Texas Instruments in 1958.

questions.prompt: Who invented the Geiger counter?
questions.explanation: Hans Geiger developed the radiation detector that bears his name.

questions.prompt: Who devised the Richter scale for earthquakes?
questions.explanation: Charles Richter introduced the magnitude scale in 1935.

questions.prompt: Who devised the Mohs scale for mineral hardness?
questions.explanation: Friedrich Mohs created the 1-10 hardness scale for minerals in 1812.

questions.prompt: Who proposed the Big Bang theory?
questions.explanation: Georges Lemaitre first proposed that the universe began with a primeval explosion.

questions.prompt: Who was the first person to walk in space?
questions.explanation: Alexei Leonov made the first spacewalk in 1965.

questions.prompt: Who invented the electrocardiograph (ECG)?
questions.explanation: Willem Einthoven invented the electrocardiograph and won a Nobel Prize for it.

questions.prompt: Who introduced the Celsius temperature scale?
questions.explanation: Anders Celsius proposed the centigrade scale in 1742.

questions.prompt: Who introduced the pH scale?
questions.explanation: Soren Sorensen introduced the pH scale in 1909 to express acidity.

questions.prompt: Who discovered infrared radiation?
questions.explanation: William Herschel found infrared rays beyond the red end of the spectrum in 1800.
